title: BTC/ETH long-or-cash timing: four economically motivated hypotheses
why: The user trades only BTC and ETH, spot, own money. Short-horizon setups and the multi-coin trend strategy failed out of sample. This tests daily long-or-cash timing on the two coins, including a data source never used for prediction here: the 6-year funding-rate history (crowding of leveraged longs and shorts).
timing: position for day d (00:00-24:00 UTC) decided only from data up to the close of day d-1; funding settlements counted only if at or before that close

hypotheses.H1_FUND_LOW: 7-day mean funding below its 20th percentile of the prior 365 days (shorts crowded) -> long for the next 7 days, else cash
hypotheses.H2_FUND_NOT_HIGH: long unless 7-day mean funding is above its 80th percentile of the prior 365 days (longs crowded) -> cash
hypotheses.H3_TSMOM28: decided on Mondays: long for the week if the Sunday close is above the close 28 days earlier, else cash
hypotheses.H4_SMA200: long if the previous close is above the 200-day simple average of closes, else cash

windows.note: signals need 365 days of funding history, so both windows start from 2021; the funding archive ends 2026-08-31

costs: 0.2% of position value per switch (0.4% round trip), no funding (spot)
statistic: timing edge = mean daily return while long minus mean daily return while in cash (computed exactly as mean of (in - p)*r / (p(1-p)))

adopt_rule.discovery: timing edge > 0 with Romano-Wolf adjusted p < 0.10 across all 8 tests (4 hypotheses x 2 assets), 30-day blocks
adopt_rule.confirmation: timing edge > 0 AND the strategy's Sharpe after costs >= buy-and-hold Sharpe
adopt_rule.CONSISTENT: edge > 0 in both windows without meeting the full rule: reported, not adopted

also_reported: strategy vs buy-and-hold CAGR, max drawdown and time in market per window; descriptive charts
no_changes_after_seeing_results: hypotheses, parameters, windows, costs and the rule above are fixed
